scope: Name alphabet letters and associate each with its usual sound.
evidence: Adult sound and letter check for all 26.

scope: Recognise letter groups for consonant and vowel digraphs and trigraphs.
evidence: Hear and match th, sh, ch, ai, ee and igh.

scope: Blend adjacent consonant sounds without dropping either sound.
evidence: Listen to a learner read brush and sand.

scope: Read verbs ending in s, ed and ing.
evidence: Read the forms in a sentence aloud.

scope: Decode regular words using letter–sound knowledge.
evidence: Read unfamiliar decodable CVC words aloud.

scope: Sound out parts of new words.
evidence: Observe how a child attempts a new word.

scope: Begin recognising common regular and exception words on sight.
evidence: Sample isolated words and the same words in a passage.

scope: Find usual written spellings for heard sounds.
evidence: Dictate sounds without displaying the options.

scope: Choose spellings for adjacent consonants and consonant digraphs.
evidence: Dictate and check both sounds and shared spellings.

scope: Connect rhyming words to recurring spellings.
evidence: Say and compare a rhyme family.

scope: Use noun plurals in s and es and explain the change in meaning.
evidence: Write labels for one and several items.

scope: Choose plausible sound spellings for simple and attempted words.
evidence: Keep an independent writing sample.

scope: Accurately spell familiar words including exceptions.
evidence: Check familiar words in unprompted writing.

scope: Get spelling help and retain useful entries in a personal log.
evidence: Inspect a log and observe later reuse.

scope: Show initial understanding of words and sentences read.
evidence: Match a sentence to an action or explain it.

scope: Use an illustration to work out what an unfamiliar word means.
evidence: Explain the picture clue after attempting to decode the word.

scope: Collect useful or interesting words from reading for writing.
evidence: Point to a word in a source text and record it.

scope: Say the alphabet in sequence.
evidence: Listen to complete oral recital.

scope: Explore sounds and words such as rhyme and rhythm in reading.
evidence: Join in and explain sound patterns.

scope: Reread with awareness of sentence boundaries and links among word groups.
evidence: Hear rereading and ask what each word group does.

scope: Explain full stops and different jobs of capitals in texts.
evidence: Find examples of names, I and sentence starts.

scope: Locate individual sentences in a text.
evidence: Mark sentence boundaries.

scope: Notice and explore sentences joined with and.
evidence: Show both joined parts.

scope: Explore how verbs and word order make statements work.
evidence: Repair a scrambled statement and explain.

scope: Find nouns and verbs in text.
evidence: Point to examples and identify their jobs.

scope: Explore when a, an and the are used.
evidence: Explain first and subsequent references to an object.

scope: Use words appropriate to a familiar topic.
evidence: Describe an object using precise words.

scope: Begin using familiar storytelling phrases.
evidence: Use a suitable opening in an original story.

scope: Draw on a personal word list to vary writing.
evidence: Compare the list and a description.

scope: Start and end a sentence with a capital and full stop.
evidence: Write an independent sentence.

scope: Use full stops for some sentences in longer writing.
evidence: Review a short passage.

scope: Capitalise I, names and some sentence beginnings in longer work.
evidence: Review a short passage including I and a name.

scope: Write simple sentences.
evidence: Write about a familiar picture or event.

scope: Join words and clauses with and.
evidence: Write one example of each joining pattern.

scope: Choose appropriate articles in sentences.
evidence: Write about first and later mentions.

scope: Discuss how events run from beginning to middle to end.
evidence: Reorder and retell an illustrated narrative.

scope: Recognise structures across fiction, non-fiction and simple poetry.
evidence: Compare features across several text types.

scope: Recognise a book's cover, title and contents.
evidence: Locate a chosen part in a real book.

scope: Notice how appearance and images vary with a text's purpose.
evidence: Explain contrasting visual features.

scope: Order and extend a short sequence of familiar events or actions.
evidence: Sequence captions and add a new event.

scope: Use basic organisation suitable for the form of writing.
evidence: Create a heading and labelled diagram.

scope: Explore stories and poems including what images contribute.
evidence: Read examples and explain an image clue.

scope: Identify features typical of simple stories.
evidence: Name characters, setting and key events.

scope: Explore different simple non-fiction forms.
evidence: Read recount, instructions and information examples.

scope: Identify some purposes and features of non-fiction forms.
evidence: Select an appropriate form for a reader's purpose.

scope: Find meanings that are directly stated.
evidence: Point to the line that answers a question.

scope: Orally retell most relevant parts of a familiar story.
evidence: Listen to the retelling without answer tiles.

scope: Recognise main characters and describe what happens to them.
evidence: Explain an event for a chosen character.

scope: Retrieve information in labels, lists and captions.
evidence: Find information in each of the three formats.

scope: Explore meanings that require clues beyond direct statements.
evidence: Offer a supported interpretation.

scope: Predict what may happen next.
evidence: Make a plausible prediction before revealing the ending.

scope: Infer meaning from story events.
evidence: Explain one inference with an event clue.

scope: Answer simple questions orally after reading or listening.
evidence: Observe both read and heard examples.

scope: Explain some reasoning when answering text questions.
evidence: Record an answer and the clue that supports it.

scope: Join in with rhyme and repeated parts with understanding.
evidence: Hear the learner anticipate and join the refrain.

scope: Begin composing simple stories and poems using familiar forms.
evidence: Collect a short story and a patterned poem.

scope: Say ideas or sentences aloud to plan writing.
evidence: Observe oral planning before writing.

scope: Write a brief retelling, for example with picture captions.
evidence: Read a sequence of captions independently written.

scope: Begin choosing writing language and features for a purpose.
evidence: Write simple instructions and a short information text.

scope: Include suitable facts in familiar non-fiction writing.
evidence: Check that facts fit the purpose.

scope: Engage with stories, poems and non-fiction read or heard.
evidence: Offer a choice and discuss responses across forms.

scope: Contribute familiar words or phrases in shared reading.
evidence: Hear participation in familiar texts.

scope: Read a simple text aloud independently.
evidence: Listen to a new short text without adult prompting.

scope: Discuss preferences and links to personal experience.
evidence: Ask for a preference and a personal connection.

scope: Start choosing books for pleasure, including listening choices.
evidence: Observe a choice and ask why.

scope: Compare story events and settings with real life.
evidence: Discuss a realistic and an imaginary event.

scope: Develop an effective and comfortable pencil hold.
evidence: Observe grip and comfort during actual writing.

scope: Form capital and lower-case letters correctly.
evidence: Inspect writing and starting movements.

scope: Join selected letters, including letter groups for sounds.
evidence: Observe appropriate joins or linked strokes with an approved model.

scope: Record simple text answers, for example as a list.
evidence: Check independently recorded answers.

scope: Present work in varied forms including labelled images and captioned panels.
evidence: Collect examples across writing and digital work.

scope: Read one's writing aloud and discuss it.
evidence: Hear a read-back and an explanation.

scope: Speak clearly enough for familiar listeners.
evidence: Listen to a short exchange.

scope: Supply information that matters to the listener.
evidence: Ask a partner to act on the information supplied.

scope: Use suitable words about feelings and events.
evidence: Hear a brief recount with a feeling.

scope: Use some communication beyond spoken words.
evidence: Observe gesture or expression without requiring eye contact.

scope: Show awareness of listeners through tone or response to cues.
evidence: Observe an adjustment during a pair talk.

scope: Listen and respond, including to a sequence of instructions.
evidence: Adult gives an unseen oral sequence and observes actions.

scope: Ask short questions about something heard or read.
evidence: Collect a learner question after each stimulus type.

scope: Work with others in a group.
evidence: Observe a shared task and contribution.

scope: Show understanding of others' opinions.
evidence: Hear the learner restate or respond to a view.

scope: Listen during discussion without interrupting.
evidence: Observe an exchange with a speaking object.

scope: Take speaking turns and share ideas and feelings.
evidence: Observe contributions in a small group.

scope: Reread sentences aloud with developing fluency and expression.
evidence: Hear two readings and compare phrasing.

scope: Recite short poems with attention to rhythm.
evidence: Listen to recitation with a steady pulse.

scope: Pause at full stops during oral reading.
evidence: Observe spoken phrasing at boundaries.

scope: Act out a simple role or imagined situation.
evidence: Observe role-play.

scope: Make a brief personal statement in a familiar setting.
evidence: Listen to a short introduction or preference.

scope: Reflect aloud on activities and what was enjoyable.
evidence: Hear a personal reflection.

scope: Suggest how gesture or expression may show feelings.
evidence: Ask about observable clues and allow alternatives.
